body.statement: If \(\binom{R+2}{2}\le\ell+3\), then there is a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\), contained in the image of legal finite-support parameter points, such that every \(\zeta\) in that subset has a curve in the nonempty fiber \(F_{\ell,R}(\zeta)\) along which \(\beta\) varies. Consequently \(L_{\ell}\le r_{\beta}(\ell)\le U_{\ell}\) and \(r_{\beta}(\ell)/\sqrt{2\ell}\to1\).
body.justification: The lower bound is robust on a legal moment chart rather than resting on one algebraic or nonreal witness.
body.gap: Neither the anchor nor generic dimension counting constructs real independent-source unequal-effect fibers on an open legal region.
body.consumer: The asymptotic square-root frontier determines how the minimum data moment order scales with latent complexity.
